Entries.Text: What this view edits: textures (TPF containers), or the menu and HUD screens (Scaleform .gfx movies).
The texture containers, by category. The File List, Texture List, Viewer and Properties show the selected TPF and texture.
The menu and HUD screens (Scaleform .gfx movies). Select one to open it: the File List shows its display list, the Texture List its images, the Viewer its stage, and Properties the selected element.
Select a movie in the Container List.

The instances on the stage at the shown frame: [depth] instance name (character). Sprites have their own timelines. Greyed-out instances aren't drawn (hidden, masks, transparent, or inside one of those).
Show every instance hidden in the preview.
Hide everything in the preview (the eye toggles show them again).

Show or hide this instance and its contents in the preview. Preview only: the movie isn't changed.

Shift+click: apply the same state to every instance of the same character.

Hidden by an instance above it. Click to hide it individually as well.

Shift+click: apply the same state to every instance of the same character.

The movie's external images. The game finds each .tga name as a cell of a shoebox layout (sblytbnd) with the same name in the TPF next to the layout, or as a texture with that name in the menu TPFs. Red means not found.
Look up the images again, after editing a layout or a menu TPF, or changing files outside Smithbox.
No shoebox cell or menu texture has this name.
The selected instance. Moves apply to the keyframes of its animation track (see Move whole animation); scale and rotation apply to the shown keyframe.
Instance names and frame labels are read-only by default. The game finds elements by instance name path (PlayerHUD/Gauge/AP_Gauge) and plays states by frame label.
Renaming an instance or a label the game uses breaks that screen without an error, because the game just stops finding it.
Click an element on the stage, or an instance in the Display List.
The instance name. The game finds elements by it.
The instance name path from the root, as the game addresses it. Unnamed levels are shown as [depth]. Right-click to copy.
The timeline the instance is placed on. An instance inside a sprite symbol is shared, so editing it changes every use of that symbol.
Sprite {0}, used {1} times. Edits change every use
Effects the stage doesn't draw yet. They are kept unchanged in the file.
Mask for the depths up to {0} (not drawn)
On: a move shifts every keyframe of the instance's animation track, so the animation plays where you put it. Off: only the shown keyframe moves, which changes the animation's path.
Position in the parent's space, in pixels.
Applies only to the shown keyframe. Skew isn't kept.
The position of the instance and its contents on the stage, in pixels.
Colour = colour x Mult / 256 + Add, per channel. Edits the keyframe that set the colour (or else the shown one).
Sprite {0}: {1} frame(s), placed {2} time(s). The shown frame applies to every use of this sprite.
The frame to show this sprite at (preview only; the game picks it at runtime).
The game plays states by frame label.
The shown frame of the root timeline.
A text field definition: edits change every instance of it. The game sets the shown text at runtime, so the initial text is mostly a placeholder.
The text box in the instance's space, in pixels.
The text in the file (HTML for HTML fields). The game usually replaces it.
An image definition: edits change every instance of it.
The image the game shows: a shoebox cell or menu texture with this name (the .tga extension is ignored).
DefineShape{0}, first fill: {1} {2}. The stage draws the shape's bounds with its first fill.
Fit the stage in the window.

Click: select the element (its nearest named instance). Ctrl+click: select the image, text or shape itself. Drag: move. Escape while dragging: cancel. Arrow keys: nudge 1 px (Shift: 10). Backspace: select the parent. Wheel: zoom. Middle-drag or Space+drag: pan.
{0}: {1} tag(s) couldn't be decoded, so they are kept unchanged (not editable).
Failed to read the menu TPF {0} for the movie images
The movie edit failed and was undone.

Images to show instead of placeholders in the GFx mode's preview: images the game fills in at runtime (MENU_Icon_00000, EquipPanel_00001) or that no atlas has. Preview only: the movies aren't changed. Saved with the project.
The image name in the movie, without its extension (MENU_Icon_00000). * matches any characters (EquipPanel_*). An exact name takes priority over a pattern, and the more specific of two patterns wins.
A shoebox cell or menu texture name to show instead. Type part of a name to pick from the names the preview knows.
No shoebox cell or menu texture has this name, so the placeholder keeps its outline.
Add the substitute, or change the one for this placeholder. Saved immediately.
Open a movie (Container List in GFX mode) to list its placeholders.
Every image in this movie was found.
Not found. Click to use it as the placeholder.
Failed to read the Scaleform configuration {0}.
Failed to write the Scaleform configuration {0}.

Make the running game load your saved menu movies without a restart. Menus on screen reopen with the new file immediately; others use it the next time they open. Panels embedded in other menus show the change after the next scene change. The game must be launched by me3 with this project as a package, and a movie added after the game started needs one restart.
Not attached. The first reload attaches to the game and installs the reloader's hooks.
Reload edited movies in the running game each time they are saved.
Reload the movies saved since the last reload.
Reload the open movie's project file in the running game.
Open a movie (Container List in GFX mode) to reload it.
The open movie has unsaved changes. Save it first, because the game reads the file.
The open movie is the game's own file. Save an edit to put it in the project first.
List the menus the game is currently showing, by the names used to reload their movies.
When off, the reloader's hooks stay in the game but do nothing, so menu files are read the game's own way again. They are never removed from the running game.
{0} {1} isn't a supported version (supported: {2}). Nothing was written to the game.
Found the Scaleform Reloader hooks installed earlier in {0}.
me3 doesn't seem to be loaded in the game. The reloader reads the files me3 serves, so without it the game keeps its startup copies.
Scaleform Reloader hooks disabled (they stay in the game, but do nothing).
The hooks are disabled. Tick Hooks enabled to reload.
The game's menu system isn't up yet.
The game isn't updating its menus (is it paused, loading or minimized?). Try again in game.
{0}: no game menu uses that name, so it was ignored.
{0} was added after the game started. me3 only serves files that existed at launch, so restart the game once to use it.
The game didn't pick up the reload within 2 seconds (is it paused or loading?). Nothing was released. Try again in game.
{0}: not on screen. The new file is used the next time it opens.
{0}: closed before it could be reloaded. The new file is used the next time it opens.
{0}: closed but didn't reopen. It should return the next time it opens.
Failed to read the Scaleform Reloader offsets {0}.

Add an item icon by its ID: the image goes into a MENU_ItemIcon cell of the menu icon sheets (hi and low), and every menu movie with an icon page for the ID shows it on that page. One undoable change; save to write the files.
The icon ID, as used by the params (iconId). Movies hold icons in pages of 1000, so the ID's page must exist in the movies.
No movie has page {0} for this ID. Usable IDs: {1}.
{0} of {1} icon movies have this ID's page, and {2} already show this icon. Hover to see the list.
Atlas cell: in {0}. The image replaces it there (and in the low sheet).
Atlas cell: none yet. One is added (also to the low sheet).

The icon image (PNG, DDS, TGA and the other formats Texture Import reads). It is scaled to the cell: 252 × 252 on the hi sheets and 126 × 126 on the low ones. Leave empty to only update the movies for an existing cell.
The file doesn't exist or isn't an image that Texture Import can read.
The hi sheet for the new cell. Automatic uses the first icon sheet with room for it. A full sheet grows when Grow Sheet is on.

When the sheet has no room for the new cell, double it (height first, up to 8192) without re-encoding the icons already on it. The low sheet grows the same way when it is full. This is the same option as Texture Import's Grow Sheet.
Put the image into the atlas cell (hi and low), then show the icon in every movie with its page, as one undoable change.
Show the existing atlas cell's icon in every movie with its page. The atlas isn't changed.
Encoding the image into the sheets...
Atlas cells written in: {0} (+ = new cell).
Save the Texture Editor to write the sheets, layouts and movies to the project.
No hi layout has item icon cells, so there is no sheet to add the icon to.
The sheet {0} can't be read or edited.
The layout of {0} can't be edited.
{0} has no icon cell to base the new cell's size on.
